title: Follow the Contract: Black-Owned Firms and Federal Contract Dollars | At The Margins, Ep. 4
lede: Black-owned businesses received about $10.23 billion of $834 billion in federal contracts in fiscal 2025, or 1.23%, while making up about 3.4% of U.S. employer firms. Episode 4 of At The Margins follows the contract: how federal goals and set-asides work, who the 8(a) program pays, the 2025–2026 rewrite of contracting rules, Canada's missing numbers, and what the evidence says set-asides do.
keyPoints: Black-owned firms' share of federal contract dollars fell from 1.53% in FY2022 to 1.23% in FY2025 (GovSpend analysis of Fedmine data; Census ABS).
In 2024, 72.5% of a $637B contracting budget went to large corporations; ~1.5% to small Black-owned businesses (Brookings, from SBA data).
Group-owned firms are ~16% of 8(a) participants but received 67% of 8(a) dollars in FY2025 (Congressional Research Service).
2025–26: EO 14173 revoked EO 11246; DOT ended DBE presumptions; SBA suspended 1,091 8(a) firms and ended the presumption of social disadvantage for new applicants (Federal Register; SBA).
City set-asides cut the Black–white business ownership gap by 3 points (Journal of Labor Economics); Prop 209 cut California highway prices 5.6% (Marion).
